uart.signal: the committed tier-1 fixture (tests/fixtures/tier1/stm32g431rb.elf) boots on the G431 descriptor and its banner bytes reach the modelled USART sink; uart_contains asserts 'TIER1 clock PASS', 'TIER1 gpio PASS' and 'TIER1 done'
uart.lane: core-ci: cargo test -p labwired-core --test strict_onboarding (the gate EXECUTES examples/stm32g431rb/io-smoke.yaml through the CLI and fails the board if any assertion fails)

spi.gap: firmware-driven, but nothing is on the far end of the bus: the fixture writes the data register and then asserts BSY/TXE/EOT flags. No device receives a byte, so this cannot distinguish a working shift engine from one that only moves status bits.
spi.lane: core-ci / core-full (nightly 02:30 UTC + workflow_dispatch + '[full-ci]') via tier1_matrix + tier1_matrix_ratchet

i2c.gap: firmware-driven register walk only: the fixture enables I2C1, sets START/STOP and checks ISR.BUSY/TXE. No device is attached, so no address ACK or payload is proven on this exact part (the G474 sibling's Arduino INA219 ACK proof does not cover the G431 descriptor).
i2c.lane: core-ci / core-full (nightly 02:30 UTC + workflow_dispatch + '[full-ci]') via tier1_matrix + tier1_matrix_ratchet
